command_sandbox.sentence: Every command a run starts is confined by the operating system to that run's workspaces.

items.name: read_file
items.description: Read a text file (line-numbered). Oversized reads return a labeled PARTIAL chunk plus the exact continuation call (start_char).
items.when_to_use: Use to inspect exact file contents. For code, prefer analyze_code first. Prefer bounded reads; if line numbers are unknown, use search_files() first. For huge/minified files, follow the #TRUNCATION notice's start_char continuation.

examples.description: Read entire file (small files; oversized returns a labeled partial chunk)
Continue a truncated read from a character offset (minified/huge files)

items.name: write_file
items.description: Write full file content (create/overwrite/append). WARNING: mode='w' overwrites the entire file; for small edits, use edit_file().
items.when_to_use: Use to create new files or intentionally overwrite/append full content. For small edits, use edit_file().

examples.description: Overwrite an existing config file with complete new content (intentional whole-file rewrite)

items.name: execute_command
items.description: Execute shell commands safely with security controls and platform detection
items.when_to_use: When you need to run system commands, shell scripts, or interact with command-line tools

timeout.description: Seconds (max 600; values above are clamped). Time limit before the command tree is killed.

examples.description: Search for a pattern in files (grep)

items.name: local_helper_start
items.description: Start one long-lived local helper process for this run (dev server, watcher, background helper) with an optional readiness contract; sandboxed to this run's workspaces, auto-cleaned when the run ends.
items.when_to_use: When the task needs a local process that must keep running across tool calls: start a dev server, wait for it to become ready, then inspect or stop it later.

items.name: shell_exec
items.description: Run a command in a PERSISTENT shell session (cwd/env/venv persist across calls). Sandboxed to this run's workspaces when the host sets a workspace policy; NOT durable (never survives a host restart).
items.when_to_use: Multi-step shell workflows where state must persist: activate a venv then run tools in it, cd and work there, start a background process (`&`) and inspect it later. A 'new shell session' notice in output means prior state is gone.

examples.description: Create and use a venv across calls

arguments.command: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install requests

examples.description: Next call, same session: venv still active
Parallel session with its own state

items.why_disabled: persistent shell sessions escape per-call cwd confinement; explicit opt-in only (backlog 0220)
